results.notes:
The new scripts/rollback-rehearsal.sh takes <candidate-artifact> <rollback-artifact>. Its guards run before any Docker call and do not depend on --dry-run. They refuse MODEL_PLANE_PRODUCTION=1, the same artifact twice, a malformed --date, an existing evidence file, --full-copy without --source-container or against a remote DOCKER_HOST, --start-stack without --no-build, and any artifact whose own configuration carries SESSION_CORE_MIGRATION_IGNORE_MISSING. It also refuses a contract migration with no revert file, and a running `model-plane` compose project, which has to be a second host or a stopped dev stack. --dry-run reads the two artifact trees, prints the migration plan and where the evidence would go, and neither verifies signatures nor calls Docker.

A real run goes in this order:
1. It verifies and restores both artifacts through their own release-artifact.sh. The candidate is verified in release mode; the rollback is verified as a plain signed artifact, because the baseline is built in non-release mode.
2. It starts a disposable Postgres from the candidate's POSTGRES_RELEASE_IMAGE, on a private network with data on tmpfs and no published port. The password is generated at run time into a 0600 temp env file and never echoed.
3. It builds the candidate schema from the candidate's own session-core migrations, or from a schema-only dump of --source-container (--full-copy copies the rows as well, local daemon only). --seed-sql adds synthetic rows. Each migration it applies is recorded in `_sqlx_migrations` with sqlx's checksum (SHA-384 of the file) and description.
4. It runs the rollback artifact's session-core image against that database. The strict boot must refuse with "previously applied but is missing" when the candidate has migrations the rollback lacks, and must boot when the sets are equal.
5. For a contract migration the script runs its `revert/*.down.sql` newest first and deletes its `_sqlx_migrations` row, then expects a strict boot. For additive-only extras it expects a boot with the switch set. Only that one container gets `SESSION_CORE_MIGRATION_IGNORE_MISSING=true`, as a literal `-e` argument. The test asserts the strict run does not carry it and that exactly one container does.
6. It runs `compose <rollback> config`, optionally `deploy` of the rollback artifact (needs --no-build and --start-stack, and leaves the stack running), and `validate-deployability` of the candidate.
7. It writes `docs/compliance/evidence/rollback-rehearsal-<date>.txt` (or --evidence-file) with names, revisions, manifest hashes, versions, counts and pass/fail only. The evidence file is also written when a run fails.

The test file sources the script, which has a main guard, for the pure helpers (`rollback_plan`, `sqlx_description`, `sqlx_checksum_hex`). It then runs the CLI against fixture artifact trees and a stub docker. Flows covered: additive extra with the switch, contract extra with scripted revert and no switch, equal sets booting strict, a strict boot that wrongly succeeds, a failing verify, and --start-stack.

Both files are LF, new and untracked. The slice owns no other file. No source revision, key or runtime value is read into any output.

results.notes:
Built behind TOOL_POLICY_ENFORCED (default off, read strictly: only the literal 'true'). With it off the engine never loads a policy, so decisions are byte-identical to before. The engine, store, API, model-gateway proxy, BFF and action contracts all exist, but the two wiring edits in shared files (server.go, main.go) are lead_todo, so nothing reads the policies end to end until they land.

Semantics as built: ask/never apply to every capability, built-in or MCP, from either scope, and the strictest in force wins (an org never beats a user allow; a user ask or never stands under an org allow). allow relaxes only the risk-level ask of an mcp_tool row (capability Kind == mcp_tool) whose floor is none and whose class is within the scope ceiling (user up to external_write, org up to destructive; owner_effect and unclassified never), and only when the policy's pinned_digest equals the row's pinned digest; an allow with a stale digest is read as an ask; an allow on a built-in or on a class the scope may not relax is ignored; a denial from the review state or the capability gate is never relaxed. A relaxed allow gets the constrained medium budget. policy_source and reason are tool_policy_never/ask/allow.

Migration 0017 (the number section 4.4 reserves): tool_policies with the partial unique index on the active key, CHECKs (org scope value = org id, allow needs a 64-hex digest, reason length), and capabilities.policy_relaxable as a STORED GENERATED column (kind = 'mcp_tool'), so it is true exactly for mcp_tool rows with no writer able to set it; revert file included. The Go engine reads capEntry.Kind rather than that column (models.Capability has no field for it and models/ is not mine), so the column is today the operator-visible mirror of that rule.

API: GET /api/v1/tool-policies?capability_id=, PUT and DELETE /api/v1/tool-policies/{capability_id}[?scope=]. Writes need capability:write, a person (not a workload), an explicit non-ZDR posture (tool_policy_write_under_zdr_refused, checked before the body is read), and for scope org an admin from the signed scopes via the existing verifiedIsAdmin (the Go twin of ownership.rs is_admin_claim; vectors pinned in the test). An allow is validated server-side against the tool's own registry row (approved, CanRelax, digest equals the pinned digest). Setting twice updates in place so the policy id survives; revoke keeps the row. Every write and revoke appends a registry_audit_log row (entity_kind tool_policy) carrying scope, capability, decision and digest, never the free-text reason.

model-gateway: GET/PUT/DELETE /v1/tool-policies..., GET /v1/mcp/servers/:server_id/tools, POST .../tools/:tool/approve through proxy_to_capability_core (which already refuses non-GET under ZDR before forwarding; I added a PUT arm), with a registry-identifier check on every path segment so a decoded ../ cannot redirect the forwarded bearer. BFF mcp.rs: the same five routes, org-scope policy writes gated on is_org_admin; approve is deliberately NOT admin-gated at the BFF because the owner of a user-scoped server must be able to approve (capability-core decides owner or admin). Action contracts tools.set_policy and mcp.approve_tool (model plane, high risk, not model-executable).

depth_findings.text: Nothing has run against a real Postgres or the rebuilt org-core image: the seven TestControlLifecycleSIEM tests compile and vet clean but are skipped without CONTROL_LIFECYCLE_TEST_DATABASE_URL, and the migration (trigger, RLS, grants as org_core_app) is untested live.

The audit outbox relay is not wired until main.go gets runSIEMAuditOutbox; until then destination changes write their audit row but it is never published, so the 'durable audit row per change' is stored but not delivered.
With the flag on and an invalid or missing ORG_CORE_SIEM_SEAL_KEY the server boots and every SIEM route answers 503 instead of failing the start; boot validation needs the main.go edit.

gdpr_hard_delete_organization (003) does not know organization_siem_audit_outbox (no FK, rows carry org_id, actor id and destination host), so erasure leaves those content-free rows behind; siem_destinations itself cascades. Decide whether erasure must purge or keep them and extend the erasure function in a later migration.

GET /internal/orgs/siem-destinations is unpaginated and returns every enabled destination of every entitled org with its plaintext secret in one response; add a limit and cursor (or per-org reads) before org count grows, and consider a request-rate or metric on this route.

Sealing supports one key id at a time; a row sealed under an old key id is skipped (logged by id) by the exporter read. A rotation path (re-seal job or a key ring in ORG_CORE_SIEM_SEAL_KEY) is not built.

Plan gate: only create and switching a destination on require feature.siem_export; a destination left enabled after a plan lapse is dropped from the exporter read by the plan join, silently. Owner should confirm silent stop versus a visible state in the admin view (S6 UI).

The four compose-reading contract tests fail against the real docker-compose.yml until the lead applies the audit-core principal and gateway scope, exactly as the WS10-S2 contract tests currently fail for inference-core; the whole-module 'go test ./...' is red until both compose edits land.

event_filter is stored and validated (events/planes, 64 entries each) but nothing enforces its semantics yet; S8's exporter must apply it and its golden should gain a case with a non-empty filter delivered end to end.
org:siem:read:any is pinned to a principal literally named audit-core (siemExporterPrincipal); if S8 wants a separate exporter principal, change the constant and the compose block together.
run-isolated-control-container-e2e.sh still builds its own inline org-core registry without the SIEM scopes; extend it only when the isolated e2e should exercise the feature with the flag on.

Migration 022 (cap trigger, RLS policies, org_core_app grants, outbox constraints) and all seven TestControlLifecycleSIEM tests have never run against a real Postgres; needed before the flag is switched on.
Until the lead wires runSIEMAuditOutbox in cmd/server/main.go, destination changes commit their audit row but it is never delivered to audit-core, so the 'durable audit row per change' is incomplete.
With the flag on and a missing or invalid seal key, the server boots and every SIEM route answers 503 (it only logs). Boot validation in main.go should turn this into a startup failure.

gdpr_hard_delete_organization (003) does not purge organization_siem_audit_outbox, which has no FK. Rows carrying org_id, actor id and destination host survive erasure; decide purge versus keep and extend the erasure function in a later migration.

GET /internal/orgs/siem-destinations is unpaginated and returns every enabled destination of every entitled org with plaintext secrets in one response; add a limit and cursor before the org count grows.

updated_since returns only rows that are currently enabled, so a destination that was disabled or deleted after the cursor never appears in an incremental read; S8's exporter must do a full refresh or this needs tombstones.
Sealing supports one key id at a time; a row sealed under an older id is skipped (logged by id) by the exporter read, and no re-seal or key-ring path exists.
A destination left enabled after a plan lapse is silently dropped from the exporter read by the plan join; confirm silent stop versus a visible state in the admin view (S6 UI).
event_filter is stored and validated but its semantics are not enforced or tested end to end; S8's exporter and golden need a non-empty-filter delivery case.
Server.SetSIEMDestinations is only called from tests (NewServer sets s.siem directly), so it is a test-only seam in production code.
org:siem:read:any is pinned to a principal literally named audit-core (siemExporterPrincipal); if S8 gives the exporter its own principal, change the constant and the compose block together.

results.notes: Built: migration 022 (siem_destinations with RLS, org_core_app grants, kind/url/ciphertext checks, revision, a trigger capping 3 per org; sibling table organization_siem_audit_outbox because the GDPR outbox pins its subject and withholds INSERT from org_core_app, so it is not generic); AES-256-GCM sealer bound by AAD to org+destination+key id (internal/org/siem_seal.go); service, validation (https only, no userinfo/fragment, no private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT/ULA/mapped literal, no numeric host spellings), repository with create/update/delete each writing its audit outbox row in the same scoped transaction under the org lifecycle advisory lock, exporter read (unscoped pool, enabled + entitled orgs only, secret unsealed, bad-key rows skipped and logged by id), FlushSIEMAuditOutbox; handlers owner/admin by membership table (forwarded role ignored), 402 plan_upgrade_required on create or switching on for a non-enterprise plan (turning off, editing and deleting never gated), PATCH needs expected_revision (409); scopes org:siem:manage:self (gateway, :self) and org:siem:read:any (pinned to principal audit-core in validateServiceCredential; placed before the generic one-segment internal read so org:read:any cannot open it); computed feature.siem_export appended to entitlements only when the feature is enabled; all five routes registered behind a 404 gate while ORG_SIEM_DESTINATIONS_ENABLED is off (internal path is always registered so it cannot fall through to /orgs/:orgId). Golden + sha256 pin vendored for the S8 client. Scripts: AUDIT_ORG_CORE_SERVICE_TOKEN minted, ORG_CORE_SIEM_SEAL_KEY (base64 of 32 bytes) and key id persisted, release preflight checks the token and (only when the flag is on) the seal key. No file was committed, staged or reverted; no docker was run.
